title: Flight count balance: old 4/2 failure and current export proof

expectation.example: The owner-provided 2026-10-05 export had assigned people with 4 and 2 distinct flights.
expectation.expected: For the people included in the balance comparison, the maximum minus minimum distinct-flight count is at most 1.
expectation.unchanged: A person holding multiple positions on one flight counts once; qualification, time, fatigue, KE166, and vacancy rules remain in force.
expectation.fallback: If safe balancing is impossible, leave the affected position unfilled with structured evidence rather than breaking the hard rule.

reproduction.reason: The old owner-provided export was independently counted by person and normalized flight number: counts included 4 and 2, spread 2.

evidence.summary: Independent count of the pre-fix 2026-10-05 export; SHA-256 recorded.

normalPath.reason: The current flight-count, optimizer, and feedback tests pass on the current source.

evidence.summary: Three focused test files passed, 82 tests total.

alternatePath.reason: The focused suite covers large candidate sets and the balance fallback path.

evidence.summary: Large candidate set and unavoidable-vacancy regression tests passed.

postProcessing.reason: The current generation and export path was run with a real local configuration; the generated artifact was checked after all scheduling finalization.

evidence.summary: Current-code export generated from the local configuration and independently counted after export.

finalGuard.reason: The focused regression suite covers final spread, post-processing rebalance, and balance-caused vacancies; the current exported artifact measured spread 1.

evidence.summary: Final spread and post-processing regression tests passed.

unchanged.reason: The current full verification evidence passed and no surrounding rule contract was changed by this acceptance update.

evidence.summary: Current full verify output: typecheck, tests, performance tests, and build passed.

finalArtifact.reason: A current-code schedule workbook was generated from the local configuration and independently checked; browser page acceptance was not used as a substitute.

evidence.summary: Generated workbook hash, input hash, assignment count, and independent per-person flight counts are recorded.

answers.originalFailure: The old export is proven to have spread 2 (4 versus 2) under the one-person-one-flight counting rule.
answers.laterChanges: The current regression suite covers normal, large-candidate, post-processing, final-guard, and vacancy fallback paths.
answers.finalArtifact: The current-code export generated from the local configuration has participant counts 2 or 3 and spread 1; its input and output hashes are recorded in the evidence file.

review.missedScope: The first fix only corrected a local counting path; it did not prove the complete finalized assignment and export path. The current check includes both.
review.rootCause: The acceptance proof was narrower than the user-visible result: local tests were treated as completion without independently recounting the final exported artifact.
review.earlyDetection: Before delivery, run the focused reverse regression, generate the real export from the target configuration, and independently deduplicate each person's exported flight numbers before recording the version fingerprint.
